name: Stalinism
summary: Stalinism is the system of rule built in the Soviet Union under Joseph Stalin from the late 1920s to 1953. It combined socialism in one country, a planned state-owned economy, forced collectivization and rapid industrialization with a one-party state, a personality cult and mass repression justified by an intensifying class struggle. Its adherents present it as Marxism-Leninism.
scope: The Soviet system of 1927-1953 under Joseph Stalin, as the defining reference works describe it (Britannica, the Library of Congress country study, the Marxists Internet Archive glossary) and as its 1936 Constitution sets it out. Answers rest on the regime's record (sources tagged action) and on the 1936 Constitution; Stalin's own speeches and works are not cited because no defining source names them. It excludes Trotskyism, Maoism, Hoxhaism and post-1956 de-Stalinised Marxism-Leninism.

vanguard-party.rationale: The doctrine of the monolithic party was central to Stalinism and the party was subjugated to its leader (s8, s10).

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: Article 135 of the 1936 Constitution gives the vote to citizens who have reached the age of eighteen (s7).

notes: Later pass under rules 7 (2026-11-14). The Wikipedia summary no longer supports any answer: its answers were re-sourced on the record (Library of Congress country study, Britannica) or the 1936 Constitution, or nulled (71 of them plus others whose only support was words not tied to the ideology). Stalin's own works (1939 Report, Economic Problems of the USSR, Dizzy with Success, Foundations of Leninism, Dialectical and Historical Materialism) were downloaded and read but fail the source tie check, since no defining source in the library names them by title twice, so no current answer cites them; a defining source naming them would let them back in. Themes searched: economy, government, religion, family, nationalities, war and foreign policy, security, rights. Encyclopedia.com refused scripted access and Ernest Mandel's 1952 essay would not download; both named here for the maintainer. The earlier missing statement (state strengthens under encirclement) is now covered by the statement state-strengthens-encirclement.

keyFigures.role: Soviet leader who defined the doctrine and system
keyFigures.quote: The political tenets of Stalinism revolve around the theory of socialism in one country–developed by Stalin to counter the Bolshevik theory that the survival of the Russian Revolution depended on proletarian revolutions in Europe.
